title: Treatment of Certain Payments in Eugenics Compensation Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the Senate on November 30, 2015. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Treatment of Certain Payments in Eugenics Compensation Act

(Sec. 2) This bill excludes payments made under a state eugenics compensation program from classification as income or resources for purposes of determining the eligibility of a recipient of such compensation for, or the amount of, any federal public benefit. The bill defines "state eugenics compensation program" as a state program for compensating individuals who were sterilized under the authority of the state.

summary.headline: This law says certain state payments to people who were forcibly sterilized will not count as income or assets when deciding their eligibility for federal benefits.
summary.what_it_does: The law excludes payments made under a state eugenics compensation program from being counted as income or resources. A state eugenics compensation program is a state program that pays people who were sterilized under state authority. Because of this rule, those payments should not reduce federal benefits or make a person ineligible for them.

who_it_affects.group: People who were sterilized under state eugenics laws and receive state compensation
who_it_affects.how: Their state compensation payments are not counted as income or resources when federal agencies decide whether they qualify for, or how much they receive from, federal public benefits.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that administer public benefit programs
who_it_affects.how: They must not treat qualifying state eugenics compensation payments as income or resources when they determine eligibility or benefit amounts.

who_it_affects.group: State governments that run eugenics compensation programs
who_it_affects.how: Payments they make under those programs are shielded from being counted against recipients' federal benefits.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The summary does not state a specific effective date, so the timing is not specified in the source material.
